paragraphs: Multi-agent systems often depend on custom roles and carefully written messages for each task. Agent Primitives treats their internal workflows as compositions of reusable components. The authors identify recurring computation patterns and implement three building blocks: Review, Voting and Selection, and Planning and Execution. This makes the unit of reuse an interaction pattern rather than an entire task-specific system.

The components communicate through the model’s key–value cache, carrying internal representations between stages. This design aims to reduce the information degradation that can accumulate through repeated natural-language exchanges. An Organizer agent chooses and combines the components for each query, consulting a lightweight collection of configurations that worked previously.

Experiments report average accuracy improvements of 12.0–16.5% over single-agent baselines. Compared with text-based multi-agent systems, token use and inference latency fall by approximately three to four times. The resulting systems still incur 1.3–1.6 times the overhead of single-agent inference. Together with greater stability across model backbones, these findings support reusable latent communication as a practical way to organize collaborative computation.
icml-2026-agent-primitives-reusable-late.tldr: Reusable agent components that communicate through KV caches improve accuracy while reducing the cost of text-based multi-agent collaboration.

paragraphs: Generating useful reasoning problems involves balancing difficulty with correctness. Strong constraints can keep problems valid but restrict their complexity; loosening those constraints can produce inconsistent or unsolvable examples. Agentic Proposing addresses this tension by treating problem creation as a sequence of purposeful decisions made by a specialized agent.

The agent selects and combines modular reasoning skills, revises its work through internal reflection, and uses tools during generation. The authors train Agentic-Proposer-4B with Multi-Granularity Policy Optimization to produce verifiable training trajectories in mathematics, coding, and science. The approach makes synthesis an iterative construction process rather than a single attempt to write a difficult question and solution.

Downstream solvers trained on the generated data outperform the reported leading baselines and generalize across domains. A 30B solver trained on 11,000 synthesized trajectories reaches 91.6% accuracy on AIME25, a result the authors describe as state of the art and competitive with frontier proprietary models. This provides evidence that carefully constructed synthetic reasoning data can deliver substantial training value from a relatively small collection.
icml-2026-agentic-proposing-enhancing-la.tldr: A specialized agent composes reasoning skills into verifiable synthetic training data that substantially improves downstream reasoning models.

paragraphs: This paper studies how large a standard Transformer must be to approximate sequence-to-sequence functions, and what statistical guarantees follow when it learns from dependent observations. Its approximation results cover targets with specified regularity: Hölder continuity with exponent between zero and one, or membership in a first-order Sobolev class. These assumptions define the function families covered by the theory.

The authors establish error bounds across all Lp norms, including the maximum-error endpoint under softmax attention. For error ε, their constructions use parameter counts scaling as ε raised to −d_x n/γ for Hölder targets and −d_x n for Sobolev targets. These match the best known scalings in the combined input dimension d_x n.

The regression analysis considers stationary covariates whose temporal dependence weakens under a beta-mixing assumption. For a sliding-window empirical risk minimization procedure, it gives excess-risk guarantees for Transformer estimators. Thus the contribution connects representational capacity with learning from sequential data, while clarifying attention’s role and supporting extensions beyond softmax.
icml-2026-approximation-bounds-for-trans.tldr: The paper derives Transformer approximation bounds and regression guarantees for regular target functions and temporally dependent data.

paragraphs: Diffusion sampling repeatedly evaluates a neural model while following a reverse-time trajectory. Higher-order numerical solvers are commonly used to reduce the number of evaluations needed for good samples. This paper asks whether another choice—the locations along the trajectory where the model is evaluated—can improve generation even when the solver remains first order.

The proposed F-DPMSolver requires no training and approximates a forward-value evaluation with a cheap one-step lookahead predictor. Its leading discretization error has the opposite sign to DDIM’s. The theoretical analysis shows that the implemented sampler approximates the ideal forward-value trajectory while retaining first-order convergence; its advantage does not come from changing its convergence order.

On standard image-generation benchmarks, the method consistently improves sample quality at the same neural evaluation budget. It is competitive with higher-order samplers and sometimes performs better. These empirical results are especially relevant when few model evaluations are available: formal solver order alone does not determine sample quality in that regime, and evaluation placement offers an additional design choice.
icml-2026-are-first-order-diffusion-samp.tldr: A training-free first-order diffusion sampler improves low-budget generation by changing where model evaluations occur along the sampling trajectory.

paragraphs: Biological neural networks commonly have heavy-tailed distributions of synaptic weights, but the computational significance of that pattern is unclear. This paper investigates its relationship to generalization in recurrent neural networks trained on cognitive tasks. The authors introduce an optimization algorithm based on optimal transport that incorporates heavy-tailed weight statistics together with biological constraints, including Dale’s principle.

Their theoretical analysis and numerical experiments identify two complementary explanations for the gains. First, heavy-tailed connectivity produces an effectively low-rank network structure and correspondingly low-dimensional neural dynamics. Second, it organizes representations of task variables near a linear manifold. That geometry makes the representations more favorable for a linear readout to generalize.

The constrained networks show substantially improved generalization across the studied cognitive tasks, with the behavior further characterized through a PAC-Bayes analysis. The contribution therefore goes beyond reporting a benefit from biological realism: it connects the weight distribution to both the dimensionality of network activity and the geometry of learned representations, offering mechanisms for the observed improvements.
icml-2026-biologically-plausible-heavy-t.tldr: Biologically constrained recurrent networks with heavy-tailed weights generalize better through low-dimensional dynamics and representations suited to linear readouts.

paragraphs: Sparse autoencoders aim to explain language-model activations using a small number of active, interpretable features. As their feature dictionaries grow, a coherent concept can become fragmented across several latents, while a broad feature can acquire arbitrary exceptions. These problems, called splitting and absorption, make an individual latent less dependable as an explanation.

The paper links both failures to inconsistent assignments across examples. Optimizing each example separately can allow the same concept to be represented by different redundant or interfering latents. Cross-sample Consistency Regularization, or C²R, adds a batch-level constraint by penalizing co-activation among latents with similar directions. This encourages a semantic feature to use a unified latent across samples.

The evaluations show that the regularizer mitigates both splitting and absorption while preserving reconstruction fidelity. That combination matters because clearer features would be less useful if they stopped accurately representing the original activations. The reported results support cross-sample consistency as a way to improve interpretability without sacrificing the autoencoder’s reconstruction performance.
icml-2026-c-2-r-cross-sample-consistency.tldr: A cross-sample regularizer makes sparse autoencoder features more consistent while preserving reconstruction fidelity.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models can generate multiple tokens in parallel, but token dependencies complicate decisions about which predictions to accept together. Conservative confidence thresholds help manage this joint dependence error, yet they also leave the model performing redundant denoising iterations. DC-Leap targets faster decoding when predictions have moderate confidence.

Its Dynamic Contiguous Verification mechanism introduces strictly ordered causal constraints into parallel decoding. By progressively checking token dependencies, it addresses the joint probability dependence error that motivates conservative acceptance. A draft also helps the decoder advance across several tokens, extending the context available for subsequent decisions. This lookahead is designed to preserve the structural advantages of bidirectional attention during inference.

The framework requires no additional training. Experiments report speedups of up to 53.19 times on MBPP for long-sequence generation, and up to 105.02 times when combined with KV caching, with comparable generation quality. These are reported maximum gains in the evaluated settings. The central finding is that dependency-aware verification can unlock more aggressive parallel progress without the reported quality loss.
icml-2026-dc-leap-training-free-accelera.tldr: DC-Leap accelerates diffusion language models through dependency-aware token verification and draft-guided jumps, without additional training.

paragraphs: An image can look convincing while failing to follow a detailed description. DetailMaster evaluates this problem using long prompts with demanding combinations of characters, scene properties, locations, and relationships. Its expert-validated prompts average 284.89 tokens, and the benchmark comes with an automated construction pipeline and an evaluation workflow.

The evaluation separates four dimensions: character attributes, structured character locations, multidimensional scene attributes, and spatial or interactive relationships. This organization helps expose whether a model preserves the connections between details, rather than merely including some requested elements. Tests cover both general-purpose image generators and models specifically optimized for long prompts.

The authors find that weak text encoders struggle to retain syntactic dependencies, while diffusion models exhibit attribute leakage under dense detail requirements. Their controlled ablation study shows that, in the tested conditions, high-fidelity generation requires expanded prompt limits together with training on long prompts. The findings connect failures to both prompt representation and image generation, showing why accepting more text alone does not resolve the evaluated problem.
icml-2026-detailmaster-can-your-text-to-.tldr: DetailMaster tests whether image generators preserve the many attributes and relationships in long prompts, revealing failures beyond prompt-length limits.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts models save computation by activating only some experts for each token. Standard top-k routing always selects the same number, despite differences between tokens and layers. Top-p routing can adapt that number by accumulating routing probability until a threshold is reached, but a fixed global threshold can make computational cost difficult to control.

DTop-p combines this adaptive selection with an explicit sparsity constraint. A Proportional-Integral controller adjusts the probability threshold, while dynamic routing normalization supports different expert selections across layers. The aim is to allocate computation according to local needs while controlling overall sparsity, rather than allowing adaptive routing to expand costs unpredictably.

Experiments on language models and diffusion Transformers show improvements over both top-k routing and fixed-threshold top-p routing at matching average FLOPs to top-k. The analysis also reports strong scaling across expert granularity, total expert capacity, model size, and dataset size. These findings indicate that adaptive routing can improve the use of an existing computation budget when paired with a mechanism that regulates that budget.
icml-2026-dtop-p-moe-sparsity-controlled.tldr: DTop-p adapts expert counts across tokens and layers while controlling sparsity, improving results at the average compute cost of top-k routing.

paragraphs: Sustainable eating involves nutritional adequacy, affordability, cultural acceptability, and environmental impact. Population-level models can describe these goals, but individual adoption depends on people with different tastes and circumstances. This paper develops a personalized recommendation approach intended to connect those broader requirements with individual food preferences.

The key modeling choice is to represent sustainability through learnable constraints rather than treating it as another user preference. This gives sustainability requirements a distinct role in the decision process while still allowing recommendations to reflect personal preferences. To evaluate the approach, the authors construct SusDiet, a dataset containing about 150,000 recipes with indicators covering all four sustainability dimensions.

Experiments on SusDiet show that the method promotes more sustainable recommendations without compromising individual preference in the reported evaluation. The findings support constraint-aware recommendation as a way to reconcile several goals within personalized choices. The dataset and model also provide a quantitative framework for studying sustainable dietary interventions and informing policy, with the reported evidence coming from the dataset experiments.
icml-2026-eating-for-a-sustainable-plane.tldr: A personalized recipe recommender incorporates sustainability as learnable constraints and improves sustainable choices while preserving evaluated user preferences.

paragraphs: ECG interpretations generated by multimodal language models can sound plausible while being clinically incorrect. ECG-R1 addresses this problem by grounding interpretation in measurable evidence and explicit diagnostic procedures. Its training corpus is generated using protocols that connect ECG features to quantitative thresholds and diagnostic logic defined in monographs.

The architecture separates modalities and uses Interleaved Modality Dropout to improve consistency when either a signal or an ECG image is unavailable. This targets a different source of unreliability: dependence on receiving both forms of input. Reinforcement learning with diagnostic evidence rewards further encourages the model to support its interpretations with ECG evidence.

The paper also evaluates proprietary, open-source, and medical multimodal models, reporting quantitative evidence that severe hallucinations are widespread. That finding gives the proposed evidence-grounding mechanisms their practical motivation. The authors explicitly caution against directly trusting such outputs without independent verification. The abstract presents ECG-R1’s training and architectural strategy alongside this diagnostic evaluation, making reliability of the reasoning process central to the contribution.
icml-2026-ecg-r1-protocol-guided-and-mod.tldr: ECG-R1 combines protocol-based data, missing-modality training, and evidence rewards to target unreliable ECG interpretation.

paragraphs: On-policy distillation trains a student language model using teacher feedback along sequences the student generates itself. A common objective, reverse KL divergence, favors matching the teacher’s most confident predictions. The authors show that this mode-seeking behavior can reduce output diversity and produce unstable learning signals when the teacher considers many next tokens plausible.

Entropy-Aware On-Policy Distillation adds forward KL when teacher entropy is high. This encourages the student to cover a wider range of plausible outputs in uncertain positions, while retaining precise imitation where the teacher is confident. The objective therefore changes with teacher uncertainty while preserving the efficiency of on-policy training.

Experiments report sustained token-level entropy and lower forward KL on high-entropy tokens, indicating better diversity and alignment in those regions. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, Pass@8 gains are +1.37, +2.39, and +5.05 for the evaluated 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B Qwen3 base models. The results connect uncertainty-aware imitation with improved multi-attempt reasoning performance relative to baseline on-policy distillation.
icml-2026-entropy-aware-on-policy-distil.tldr: Adapting the distillation objective to teacher uncertainty preserves student diversity and improves multi-attempt mathematical reasoning.

paragraphs: Molecular generation must coordinate continuous atom positions with discrete chemical categories. Conventional approaches evolve these quantities in separate spaces, which the authors identify as a mismatch with their underlying statistical geometry. EvoEGF-Mol represents both through composite exponential-family distributions, putting coordinates and categories into a shared natural-parameter space.

Within that representation, the two kinds of information evolve together along exponential geodesics under the Fisher-Rao metric. Directly targeting a perfectly concentrated Dirac distribution would cause instantaneous trajectory collapse. The proposed method avoids this by using target distributions that become concentrated dynamically, together with a training architecture that progressively refines parameters.

On CrossDock, the model achieves a 93.4% PoseBusters passing rate, approaching the reference level reported by the authors. It also outperforms baseline methods on MolGenBench tasks involving recovery of bioactive scaffolds. These results support the approach’s geometric precision and interaction fidelity in the evaluated tasks. The contribution ties those outcomes to a unified probabilistic treatment of molecular position and chemical identity.
icml-2026-evoegf-mol-evolving-exponentia.tldr: EvoEGF-Mol jointly evolves atom positions and chemical categories in a unified probabilistic geometry, improving evaluated molecular generation quality.

paragraphs: Training NMR chemical-shift predictors usually requires spectra whose measurements have been assigned to individual atoms, a labor-intensive source of labels. This paper develops a semi-supervised method that combines a small labeled collection with millions of literature-extracted spectra lacking those assignments. The goal is to make much larger spectral collections usable for learning.

The method treats supervision as comparison between sets, so the order of unassigned measurements does not determine the training target. Under commonly satisfied conditions on the loss, the authors show that optimal bipartite matching reduces to a sorting-based loss. This conditional result supplies a simpler route to stable training at the scale of the literature-derived data.

The resulting models improve accuracy and robustness over the reported state-of-the-art methods and generalize more strongly across larger, more diverse molecular datasets. Incorporating solvent information at scale also captures systematic effects across common NMR solvents. The findings demonstrate a practical way to learn from weakly structured scientific records while retaining a small amount of explicit atom-level supervision.
icml-2026-from-human-labels-to-literatur.tldr: Set-based semi-supervised learning turns millions of unassigned literature spectra into useful training data for more accurate NMR shift prediction.

paragraphs: Using language models as judges requires knowing when their decisions are likely to agree with people. A hypothesis-testing approach discussed in this paper assumes that estimated confidence tracks human-disagreement risk monotonically. If confidence fails to order cases that way, its usefulness for enforcing an agreement target is weakened.

The authors train a dedicated confidence estimator using simulated annotator diversity and a margin-based ranking objective. The estimator learns to distinguish cases of human agreement from disagreement, rather than depending on heuristic confidence signals. A theoretical analysis provides generalization guarantees and identifies a margin-dependent trade-off that guides an adaptive training procedure.

When combined with fixed-sequence testing, the learned estimator improves ranking accuracy and empirically strengthens the relationship between confidence and disagreement risk. Across several datasets and judge models, the procedure more often satisfies target agreement levels. The result is an improvement in the empirical reliability of confidence-based testing; the abstract describes stronger monotonic behavior, rather than claiming that training makes monotonicity universally hold.
icml-2026-margin-adaptive-confidence-ran.tldr: A learned confidence-ranking model helps LLM judging procedures more reliably meet target levels of agreement with human judgments.

paragraphs: Tool-using language models often choose one call at a time, even when a task requires several tools with dependencies between them. NaviAgent separates the overall task decision from the details of assembling and executing tool sequences. This division is intended to make orchestration more manageable as the available tool collection grows.

At the planning level, an agent decides whether to answer directly, clarify the request, or retrieve and run a toolchain. At the execution level, a Tool World Navigation Model represents structural and behavioral relationships among tools as a graph. Feedback from actual tool interactions connects the two levels, allowing execution experience to inform subsequent navigation and planning.

Evaluations on API-Bank and ToolBench show consistent improvements in task success, with the navigation model contributing an average gain of 13.1 points on complex tasks. Tests using 50 real APIs across seven domains report gains of 4.3–12.0 points with fewer steps and lower latency. These results support modeling tool relationships explicitly when coordinating dependent operations in changing tool environments.
icml-2026-naviagent-graph-driven-bilevel.tldr: NaviAgent separates task planning from graph-guided tool execution, improving success and efficiency when coordinating dependent tools.

paragraphs: Prompt-based value alignment becomes difficult when several requested values pull in different directions. A model may follow only part of the instruction or favor some values over others. PICACO addresses this instruction bottleneck by optimizing a meta-instruction that helps a language model respond to multiple intended values together.

The approach works without fine-tuning. It maximizes total correlation between the specified values and model responses, using that objective to improve the instruction itself. The paper’s theoretical account connects this optimization to stronger value conformity and reduced distracting noise. The intended effect is to make the prompt communicate the joint value requirements more effectively.

Experiments cover five value sets and include both black-box and open-source language models. PICACO outperforms several recent strong baselines and achieves a better balance across as many as eight distinct values. These results support instruction optimization as a way to improve pluralistic alignment in the tested settings, where success depends on responding to several potentially conflicting requirements rather than satisfying a single preference.
icml-2026-picaco-pluralistic-in-context-.tldr: PICACO optimizes prompts without fine-tuning to help language models balance multiple, potentially conflicting human values.

paragraphs: When noise dominates a signal, local time–frequency observations become unreliable. Enhancement models can then suppress useful content too aggressively or leave artifacts behind. FracKGMF addresses this problem by combining a broader pattern of information aggregation with a mechanism that accounts for uncertainty when combining multiple views.

Its Fractional Distance Decay Convolution changes how local interactions weaken with distance, producing long-tailed receptive patterns. This allows the model to gather weak but mutually consistent cues beyond an ambiguous individual time–frequency bin. Knowledge Guided Multi-view Fusion then uses a Wiener-inspired reliability prior to calibrate how views are combined, reducing excessive suppression where the evidence is uncertain.

Experiments on speech and electromagnetic signal benchmarks report consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. Gains are particularly large under extreme noise, including a reported average improvement of 33 dB on electromagnetic signals at −20 dB. The findings support pairing expressive signal aggregation with reliability-aware fusion: one component collects dispersed evidence, while the other regulates decisions when that evidence remains uncertain.
icml-2026-robust-signal-enhancement-via-.tldr: FracKGMF combines long-tailed signal aggregation with reliability-guided fusion to improve enhancement under very strong noise.

paragraphs: GUI agents must carry information across multiple actions while adapting to interfaces that can change. Limited context windows make long-term planning difficult, and a fixed policy cannot continually incorporate new experience. SE-GA combines a hierarchical memory system with an iterative training process to address both problems.

During inference, Test-Time Memory Extension retrieves relevant episodic, semantic, and experiential memories. This supplies salient context for the current task without relying only on what remains in the immediate context window. A separate Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution pipeline uses the data collected through this memory-assisted activity to stabilize and improve the agent’s underlying policy.

The evaluations span offline and online benchmarks. SE-GA reports state-of-the-art performance, including success rates of 89.0% on ScreenSpot and 75.8% on AndroidControl-High, alongside significant improvements on AndroidWorld. The AndroidWorld results support better generalization to dynamic environments in the reported evaluation. The overall contribution connects memory retrieval during task execution with policy improvement afterward, so experience serves both immediate planning and subsequent learning.
icml-2026-se-ga-memory-augmented-self-ev.tldr: SE-GA uses retrieved memories for GUI task planning and turns collected experience into further policy improvements.

paragraphs: Recognizing handwritten mathematics requires understanding how symbols fit together in two dimensions. This paper introduces a benchmark spanning 13 categories of structurally complex expressions, with authentic handwriting artifacts. It tests whether large models can recover expression structure even when they are reasonably accurate at reading individual symbols.

The evaluation finds that performance deteriorates as structural complexity increases. Most errors involve misreading the structure or confusing a symbol’s role in context, rather than simply failing to see the symbol. To address those failures, the authors propose a training-free procedure that first identifies a structural schema, then transcribes within that schema, and finally resolves ambiguities using context.

On Qwen-8B, the method raises ExpRate from 11.63% to 24.52%, and the authors report that it generalizes across several large models. The improvement supports separating structural interpretation from symbol transcription. The benchmark also makes a useful diagnostic distinction: high accuracy on individual marks can coexist with much weaker recognition of the complete mathematical expression.
icml-2026-seeing-symbols-missing-structu.tldr: A handwriting benchmark exposes structural errors in mathematical recognition, and a training-free schema-guided procedure improves complete-expression recognition.

paragraphs: A vision-language model can fail at a game because it misreads the board, misunderstands a rule, or cannot predict what happens next. This paper builds a diagnostic framework to separate those possibilities. Controlled perception tests isolate visual encoding, while a six-level rule-complexity ladder compares verification of observed outcomes with prediction of future states.

Across six models, spatial mistakes are coordinated: adjacent pieces share the direction of off-by-one errors 1.5–1.9 times as often as expected under independence. The evaluation also finds a separation between perception and reasoning. At complex constraint levels, perception remains relatively stable while reasoning accuracy declines sharply, with the best-performing model reaching at most 75%.

Predicting future states produces an additional performance drop of up to 27 points compared with checking observed outcomes. Within the tested settings, scaling, text-only inputs, and structured prompting do not resolve these limitations. The results show why an overall gameplay score is insufficient to explain failure: visual localization, rule application, and simulation reveal distinct weaknesses that require separate measurement.
icml-2026-seeing-without-understanding-d.tldr: A diagnostic gameplay evaluation separates visual errors, rule-reasoning failures, and future-state prediction gaps in vision-language models.

paragraphs: Automatically optimizing a prompt for one model and one objective does not directly solve prompting in a system that routes requests among many models. Such systems must handle task differences, model differences, and competing user priorities. TAMPO learns to generate prompts conditioned on those factors so prompt optimization can support auto-routing.

The authors build a dataset designed to capture performance variation across tasks and models, then train an uncertainty-aware reward model. This model acts as an offline proxy during optimization and is intended to substantially mitigate reward hacking. A multi-objective conditional policy uses a preference vector encoding user requirements to control the prompts it generates.

Experiments across 86 tasks show stable performance across diverse tasks and models. The framework also supports a cost-effective deployment strategy through its controllable prompt policy. The contribution is therefore broader than producing a single optimized instruction: it connects prompt generation to the particular model, task, and requested trade-offs that a routed language-model system must accommodate.
icml-2026-tampo-task-and-model-aware-aut.tldr: TAMPO generates prompts conditioned on tasks, models, and user trade-offs to support stable, controllable optimization in auto-routing systems.

paragraphs: Anatomical shapes can change differently across regions, and uncertainty about those changes can vary spatially as well. PRISM addresses this heterogeneity by combining implicit neural representations with probabilistic shape analysis. Instead of relying on a global time-warping description, it models a distribution of shapes conditioned on developmental covariates.

The model supplies spatially continuous estimates of both the population mean and covariate-dependent uncertainty at arbitrary locations. This allows the representation to describe how expected anatomy and its variability differ across space. A closed-form Fisher Information metric provides an analytically tractable way to quantify local temporal uncertainty efficiently using automatic differentiation.

Experiments on three synthetic datasets and one clinical dataset demonstrate strong performance on tasks including shape evolution and anomaly detection. The authors also report interpretable, clinically meaningful uncertainty estimates. The contribution brings those tasks into one framework, connecting a flexible representation of three-dimensional shape with statistical quantities that describe where and how confidently developmental variation can be characterized.
icml-2026-textttprism-a-3d-probabilistic.tldr: PRISM models anatomical shape distributions with spatially varying means and uncertainties, supporting shape evolution analysis and anomaly detection.

paragraphs: Evaluating a driving policy in a closed loop requires a simulated world that responds as the policy acts. VectorWorld generates that world incrementally as vehicle-centered tiles containing lanes and agents. Its design addresses three obstacles identified by the authors: initialization inconsistent with past motion, generation too slow for real time, and accumulating violations of feasible movement.

A motion-aware gated variational autoencoder handles initialization using motion history. An edge-gated relational diffusion Transformer, combined with interval-conditioned MeanFlow and large-step supervision based on Jacobian-vector products, extends the scene without a sampling solver. A separate physics-aligned policy, ΔSim, controls other road users through mixed discrete and continuous actions with kinematic shaping.

On Waymo Open Motion and nuPlan, the system improves map fidelity, initialization validity, and density calibration. It supports stable real-time closed-loop rollouts extending beyond one kilometer. These findings connect scene generation speed with history compatibility and feasible motion, showing how the components work together to sustain interactive simulation over longer driving trajectories.
icml-2026-vectorworld-efficient-streamin.tldr: VectorWorld incrementally generates vector-graph driving scenes and physics-aligned traffic, enabling stable real-time rollouts beyond one kilometer.

paragraphs: Representations for spatial reasoning need to encode both what an object is and where it is located. WorldComp2D explicitly organizes its latent space around object identity and spatial proximity. It uses local receptive fields at several scales, aiming to obtain useful spatial and semantic information without relying on dense feature maps or task-specific structures.

The framework has two main components. A proximity-dependent encoder converts an observation into the structured latent representation, and a localizer infers object coordinates from that representation. Making spatial relationships part of the latent geometry gives the coordinate prediction stage a representation already organized around the information it needs.

Facial landmark localization serves as the proof of concept. Compared with state-of-the-art lightweight models, WorldComp2D reduces parameter counts by up to four times and FLOPs by up to 2.2 times while maintaining real-time CPU operation. These results demonstrate computational benefits in the evaluated localization setting and support explicitly structured latent spaces as a promising foundation for efficient spatial-semantic reasoning.
icml-2026-worldcomp2d-spatio-semantic-re.tldr: WorldComp2D explicitly organizes latent representations by identity and proximity, enabling lightweight, real-time facial landmark localization.
